integration_options.name: The hub and its rooms: My LCA holds every role as a section, each section opens its working room, the word Workspace goes
integration_options.idea: One home for everyone at /dashboard, labelled My LCA. A plain member sees You only, no chips, no role rows. Each further grant adds one section (Family, Events you direct, Your region, Board, LCA admin, Member lookup) that summarises its work, takes one-tap decisions inline, and opens its working room with one button. The rooms keep the decided paths under /workspace/... and /board/... but the word Workspace leaves the header, the menu and every breadcrumb; each room is named for what it is (Setup, Event day, Recap, My region, Board inbox, Support tickets, Member lookup) and carries 'My LCA › ...' above it. Admin stays a separate area at /admin for lca_admin only, reached from its own summary section. What a non-designer sees: one long page with buttons out to the rooms, and the same header everywhere.
integration_options.header: The decided bar on every page: Donate · My LCA ▾ with the personal to-do count (WS02; Nav-Header-Final). The menu keeps the WS02 order, with the one row 'Workspace / Admin / Board inbox / My region's clubs by role' replaced by named rooms, each with its own count in words: the to-do items; My LCA; the active event line while event mode is on; Family; Membership card; the rooms; Log out. Member (Avery): 'To do: Finish payment · Paul Morphy Open' · My LCA · Membership card · Log out. Parent (Danielle): the same plus Family (/dashboard#family); the event line reads 'November Meet · Maya and Leo's boards'. TD (Chris): plus 'Events you direct (2)' (/dashboard#directing) and, while event mode is on, 'The Baton Rouge Classic · Open event day' (/workspace/tournaments/:id/live); the tournament_director role adds 'Member lookup' (/workspace/lookup). Representative: plus 'My region · 4 to check' (/workspace/region) and 'Board inbox (3)' (/board/inbox) for the seat. Officer: plus 'Board inbox (3)' and 'Support tickets (4)' (/workspace/tickets); the president also 'Email the members' (/workspace/email). Admin: plus one row, 'Admin · 12 need attention' (/admin), after the personal rows, and any TD or seat rows they hold. Auditor: plus 'Member lookup'. No row ever reads Workspace or Admin panel.
integration_options.routes: /dashboard is My LCA with the anchors #today #you #family #directing #region #board #admin #lookup, which the On this page rail jumps to; /me/players/:memberId (WS06). The rooms keep the decided paths so WS08, WS09 and WS14 build as written, and none is titled Workspace: /workspace/tournaments/new (admins and representatives), /workspace/tournaments/:id/setup, /:id/live, /:id/recap; /workspace/region and /workspace/region/clubs/:id; /workspace/lookup; /workspace/tickets and /workspace/email (moved out of /admin for officers and the president, open for K); /board/inbox. /workspace itself redirects to /dashboard#today; /admin/tournaments/:id sends a non-admin to the setup room and /admin/clubs/:id to the club room; /manage/club goes with club_rep. /admin and /admin/:section, /admin/clubs/:id and /admin/tournaments/:id are lca_admin with a second factor. The Nav-IA-Final route table changes in two rows (Workspace and My region's clubs).
integration_options.my_lca_holds: Inline: the Today list across roles; the whole You section; Family cards, the guardians panel and the event-day view; per event the counts, flags, next step and the one-tap bye decision and reminder email; per region the clubs to check with one-tap 'Still accurate' and the open reports; the board inbox preview, next meeting and documents list; the admin queue counts, assigned items and the automations line; the one-field lookup. Anything that is a table, a grid, a reply or a multi-step form opens the room.
integration_options.stays_separate: /admin in full, lca_admin only: Members, money, Email (except the president's room), Audit, Site, Board seats, Clubs create/rename/region/delete, LCA event creation and approvals, Content, Champions, the season. Officers and the president no longer open /admin at all; what they can do becomes rooms (tickets, documents, email). The TD console, My region, the board inbox and the lookup are rooms, not admin.
integration_options.moving: Out: a section's primary button (Setup, Event day, Open My region, Open board inbox, Open Admin), a Today item's action, a room row in the menu, or on event day the strip's 'TD console' button, which deep-links so a TD at the venue never passes through the hub. The room is a full-width page under the same site header; its first line is the crumb 'My LCA › Events you direct › The Baton Rouge Classic › Event day', every crumb a link; the console keeps Work-A's 'Exit console' top right, returning to /dashboard#directing; My region, the checklist, the inbox and the lookup carry 'Back to My LCA'; after a finishing action (Publish round 4, Confirm all, Mark as submitted) a line 'Done · Back to My LCA'. Between rooms: the menu rows, never through Admin. No mode switch: one header, one account, a room is a page; only the hall TV and print leave the chrome.
integration_options.tradeoff: The page grows with every role (Chris, six sections, scrolls about 3400px at 1440 wide), so sections must collapse and remember it per device, and the Today list must be ranked well or one role's noise drowns the rest; every room needs its own crumb and back control; the rooms share no sidebar, so a representative hopping between nine clubs goes club › region › club or uses the room's own tabs; and Workspace vanishing as a word means WS08's and WS09's chrome copy is renamed while the paths stay. In return it is exactly what K wrote: a member's extra roles and their stuff live in My LCA, and nobody but an admin sees the admin panel.

integration_options.name: My LCA as an area with a left rail: the rooms are pages inside it, Admin separate
integration_options.idea: My LCA stops being one page and becomes a small area under /my with a persistent left rail: Overview · You · Family · The Baton Rouge Classic · My region · Board · Member lookup · Settings, one entry per grant the person holds. Overview is the Today list plus one short card per section; each rail entry is a full page, and the working screens (the console, the checklist, My region, the inbox, tickets, email) are pages in the same shell, so there is no 'summary here, work there' step. A plain member sees the rail with Overview and You, or no rail at all under two entries. Admin stays separate at /admin with its own sidebar. What a non-designer sees: a left rail like the admin's, short pages, no long scroll.
integration_options.header: The bar is unchanged: Donate · My LCA ▾ with the personal count. One short menu for everyone: the to-do items; My LCA (/my); the active event line; Family (/my/family); Membership card; 'Admin' (/admin) for lca_admin; Log out. The role rows leave the menu because the rail carries them. Member: to-dos · My LCA · Membership card · Log out. Parent: plus Family. TD, representative, officer and auditor: the same menu as a member; their rooms are rail entries ('The Baton Rouge Classic', 'My region', 'Board · 3', 'Member lookup'), and the event line still deep-links to /my/events/:id/live. Admin: plus 'Admin · 12'. The trigger keeps the personal count; the rail's Overview row shows the across-roles count.
integration_options.routes: /my (Overview; /dashboard redirects), /my/you, /my/family and /my/family/:memberId, /my/events (the directing list), /my/events/new, /my/events/:id/setup, /live and /recap, /my/region and /my/region/clubs/:id, /my/board (inbox, documents, email by role), /my/lookup, /my/tickets, /my/settings; /workspace/* and /board/inbox redirect into /my; /admin/* unchanged. The most rebuilt routes of the three: every decided /workspace and /board path moves, so WS08, WS09 and WS14 text and the Nav-IA-Final route table change.
integration_options.my_lca_holds: Overview holds the Today list and short cards (one or two lines each) that link to the rail pages. The rail pages hold everything the Int-A sections hold plus the working screen itself: the event page is the checklist with the counts at its top, the region page is My region, the Board page is the inbox with the documents and the president's email as tabs.
integration_options.stays_separate: /admin exactly as in Int-A. The rail never shows an Admin row; admins reach /admin from the header only. An lca_admin opening another TD's event does so from /admin › Tournaments, which opens /my/events/:id/live with the strip 'You're here as an LCA admin', the one place the two areas meet.
integration_options.moving: The rail is the movement: Overview to any room in one click and back in one; the current entry carries aria-current and a bar. The Today list's actions deep-link into a rail page. On the console and the checklist at 1024px the rail folds to icons or into a 'My LCA ▾' crumb at the left of the status band so nothing scrolls sideways; on tablets it becomes a top row of tabs; on phones it is a sheet behind the page title. The event strip's button deep-links to /my/events/:id/live. Back to Overview is the rail's first entry and the crumb 'My LCA'.
integration_options.tradeoff: Two rails on the site that look alike (the My LCA rail and the admin sidebar), which is what K wanted to get away from; the rail costs 240px that the console and the checklist cannot spare at 1024px, so they fold it and the 'same shell' promise weakens exactly where Chris works hardest; a person-centred home and task-centred screens share one URL space, so an admin backstopping an event lands under 'My' something that is not theirs; every decided route moves; and the single-role member gets a rail with two rows, which looks like an empty admin panel unless the rail hides for them, so the area looks different for different people. In return the volunteer with five roles never scrolls a long page, and each role's work has a stable URL.

integration_options.name: My LCA personal, Your work beside it: a second page holds the Today list and the rooms, Admin separate
integration_options.idea: Two homes for a volunteer, one for everyone else. /dashboard (My LCA) is personal for everyone: You and Family only, with the personal Needs attention row. /work (today's /workspace renamed 'Your work') holds the Today list across roles at the top and one card per room (Events you direct, My region, Board, Member lookup, Support tickets), with the rooms under it. A member with no grants never sees Your work. Admin stays at /admin and gets its own card on Your work for lca_admin. What a non-designer sees: a short personal page, and a second, denser page that is honestly work.
integration_options.header: The bar is unchanged for everyone: Donate · My LCA ▾ with the personal count. Menu: the to-do items; My LCA; the active event line; Family; Membership card; 'Your work · 6' (/work) for anyone holding a role, a seat or a directed event, replacing Workspace, Board inbox and My region's clubs; 'Admin · 12' (/admin) for lca_admin; Log out. Member: to-dos · My LCA · Membership card · Log out. Parent: plus Family. TD, representative, officer and auditor: plus 'Your work · n things'. Admin: plus 'Your work' and 'Admin · 12'. The trigger count stays personal; the Your work row carries its own count, a second count beside the one WS02 decided.
integration_options.routes: /dashboard stays My LCA (You, Family); /me/players/:memberId. /work is Your work; its rooms sit under it: /work/tournaments/new, /work/tournaments/:id/setup, /live, /recap, /work/region and /work/region/clubs/:id, /work/lookup, /work/tickets, /work/email; /board/inbox stays as it is, linked from the Board card; /workspace/* redirects to /work/*; /admin/* separate. One prefix renamed, no new structure.
integration_options.my_lca_holds: My LCA: the You and Family sections in full, and for role holders one quiet line under the heading, '6 things across your roles · Open Your work'. Your work: the Today list (volunteer items, with the personal items repeated so Chris's Monday is one list), the room cards with their counts and one-tap decisions, and the rooms. The role cards are the same section boards drawn as cards, so the pick costs no redraw.
integration_options.stays_separate: /admin as in Int-A, plus a cleaner line: Your work never shows personal money or family items except as the repeated Today rows, and My LCA never shows volunteer queues.
integration_options.moving: My LCA's line under the heading or the menu row leads to Your work; a card's button or a Today action opens its room; the crumb reads 'My LCA › Your work › The Baton Rouge Classic › Event day' and 'Back to Your work' sits in every room's band; the event strip deep-links to the console. The header is the same bar on both homes.
integration_options.tradeoff: K asked for My LCA to host a member's roles; this puts them one click away, and two homes read as a mode even with no switcher. Chris's Monday starts on two pages (Ella's unpaid entry on one, the bye request on the other) unless the work list repeats the personal items, and the header needs a second count to make Your work findable, against WS02's decided single personal count. In return the default page for the 300+ stays plain with nothing to hide, Your work can be dense without worrying a member, and the role cards and rooms are the same boards as Int-A.

frame.baseline: The section boards (Account-D to Account-S) and the screen boards (Work-E to Work-L) are drawn inside Account-Int-A, the hub and its rooms, with Chris (member, parent of Ella, director of The Baton Rouge Classic, South Central Louisiana representative, treasurer with the lca_officer role) as the drawn person and Avery as the plain member. Why Int-A: it is K's own sentence on Tue, Oct 13 ('a good place to host all of a members additional roles and their stuff, instead of letting them see the admin panel'), and Int-A is the only option where that sentence is literally the page: the roles are sections on My LCA, the work opens from them, and only lca_admin ever sees /admin. It keeps Account-C as the base without making it the default: a member with no grants sees You alone, no chips, the On this page rail listing the You section's parts, and nothing that hints at volunteer work. It keeps the decided chrome unchanged: the WS02 menu order stands (to-dos, My LCA, the event line, Family, Membership card, then the rooms by role, then Log out) with the one word Workspace replaced by named rooms, and the Nav-IA-Final route table changes in two rows. It keeps every URL that WS08, WS09 and WS14 already build to, so nothing is rebuilt. And it is the frame under which the two days read right: on Monday morning Chris opens My LCA, the Today list carries Ella's unpaid entry, the bye request, the four clubs to check and three board messages, and he finishes two of them without leaving the page; on tournament Sunday the live event sits first under Today with 'Round 3 · 8 of 13 results confirmed · Open event day', the strip's TD console button is one tap, and the console's band reads 'My LCA › The Baton Rouge Classic › Event day' with Exit console back to /dashboard#directing. The legend on every section and screen board says the frame is swappable, in one line: 'Drawn inside Int-A (My LCA as the hub, rooms open from each section). The frame is swappable: under Int-B this section is the page the left rail opens; under Int-C it is a card on Your work. The room itself does not change; only the breadcrumb, the way back and the menu row do. Pick the frame on Account-Int-A, B or C.' The section boards also carry the two small insets the brief asks for, the section's row in the On this page rail ('Events you direct · 3') and its row in the My LCA ▾ menu. The screen boards (Work-E to Work-L) add the three breadcrumbs side by side in the legend ('My LCA › ...', 'My LCA rail › ...', 'Your work › ...') so K can see the way in and back under each frame without a screen being redrawn.
frame.today_rules: The list is headed 'Today' with its weekday date ('Mon, Oct 5'). It reads 'Today across your roles' only when two or more roles contribute an item for this person, with a sub-line '6 things · 2 are yours' so the header's personal count never exceeds what the person sees; a plain member sees 'Today' and nothing about roles. What counts as an item: something the viewer can finish or decide today, from this page or one of its rooms, with a deadline within 14 days or a person waiting on the viewer now; it carries exactly one action button in words. A status, a count of things that are fine, or information with no action is never an item (that belongs in Next up, the section, or the event strip). What counts, per role. You: an unpaid entry before its deadline ('Pay $60 by Sat, Oct 17'); a US Chess membership ending before an entered event, from 7 days before; an LCA membership within 30 days of expiry or expired, never pending; an open waitlist offer with its claim time; a bye request answered; a reminder you set that fires today; on an event day one line per event you play ('Playing today · Round 1 at 10:00 AM · My board'). Family: the same for each child, each line starting with the child's first name ('Leo needs a US Chess ID before Sat, Nov 14'); a guardian request to approve; a child's invite not accepted after 7 days; on an event day one line per event the children play, not one per child. Director, per event named on: results needed before the next round can be paired and, on the day, reports waiting in the Reported results queue (disagreements named); a bye request pending; entrants whose US Chess membership ends before the event (one item per event with the count, from 7 days before); a setup step left before registration opens or before day 1 ('Next: publish the prize list'); 'Round times missing: players see time to be announced'; the rating report due within 7 days of the last round; 'Mark as completed' after the last result. Representative: the region's clubs not checked in 90 days (one item for the region with the count and names) or the monthly confirm due; a Suggest an update or Report outdated info with no answer (one item each, on the 14-day clock; at 14 days it is also an admin item); a club event you created still in LCA review. Board seat: messages awaiting a reply in each seat's inbox (one item per seat with the count and the oldest date); the next board meeting within 7 days, with Add to calendar or the agenda. Officer role: support tickets assigned to you; minutes not posted 14 days after a meeting (the secretary). President: nothing extra. Admin: one line for the queue ('12 items need attention in Admin · oldest 3 days'), each item assigned to this admin by name as its own line, and a failed automation; never the whole queue inline. Auditor: never an item. Ranking, in five tiers: 1, due today or already past, any role (an entry deadline today, a waitlist claim ending today, a round waiting to be paired now, a rating report due today, an expired membership); 2, money and eligibility with a date, in WS13's order (an unpaid entry, US Chess ending before an entered event, LCA membership within 30 days, a waitlist offer), then the nearer date first, so WS13's Needs attention order and its unit test stand for the personal items; 3, a person waiting on you (a bye request, reports that disagree, a guardian request, a visitor report, a ticket, a board message), longest wait first; 4, dated upkeep (the 90-day club check, a setup step before a date, the rating report within 7 days, minutes not posted, a meeting within 7 days); 5, counts and summaries (the admin queue line, inbox counts). Inside a tier the sooner deadline first, then the role order You · Family · Director · Representative · Board · Admin, so a personal item never sinks under a volunteer item of the same urgency, and no item from any role outranks a deadline that falls earlier. On an event day the live event's items form one group at the top with the event's name as the group line. Account-G draws this as one merged list; Account-H ranks the same way inside each role but groups under role headers with counts ('Director · 3', 'Family · 1') under one urgent band holding anything in tier 1 or due within 48 hours; the counting rules are the same on both. The role label: a worded chip at the start of each row, from a fixed list that names the event, child or seat and never the system role word: 'You', the child's first name ('Ella'), 'Director · The Baton Rouge Classic', 'Representative · South Central Louisiana', the seat's name ('Treasurer'), 'LCA office', 'Admin'; words beside a tint, never colour alone; when one role holds every item the labels are dropped and the heading is simply 'Today'. The empty day: never an empty box, no card, no picture. 'Nothing needs you today.' then in grey the next dated thing from Next up ('Next: The Baton Rouge Classic, Sat, Oct 24 · you're entered and paid'; for a new member with no entries 'Nothing entered yet · Find a tournament'), and for role holders one line per role with its next dated thing ('Director: Bunkie G/90 rating report due Sat, Oct 10'); the section keeps its place in the On this page rail with no count, and the header trigger shows no count. The cap: seven items open; the rest behind 'Show 4 more' (the number in words, never 'See all'), which opens them grouped by role; before the fold no role may hold more than three items, so the admin queue or a busy event cannot drown Ella's unpaid entry; nothing is ever dropped, because each role section lists all of its own items anyway. The header's My LCA count stays the personal count (unpaid entries for self and children, a membership ending or lapsed, US Chess before an entered event, capped at 9+; WS02 and Nav-IA-Final name src/lib/todo.ts, not yet in the tree), and volunteer items never count there; the role rows in the My LCA ▾ menu carry their own counts in words. An item leaves the list the moment the thing is done, with no history; nothing is dismissed by hand except the meeting line, which hides until the next meeting is set. The same providers feed the menu's to-do rows (personal items only, the WS02 order) and the role sections' flags, so one thing is never worded two ways. Every date carries its weekday, times read '7:00 PM', 'US Chess' always, status in words beside any colour.
open_for_k: Pick the frame: Int-A (My LCA as the hub, rooms open from each section; the boards' baseline), Int-B (My LCA as an area with a left rail, rooms inside it) or Int-C (My LCA personal, Your work beside it). A different pick changes only the breadcrumb, the way back and the menu row on every section and screen board.

Does the word Workspace survive? Default: no. The rooms keep today's /workspace/... paths so WS08 and WS09 build as written, but the word leaves the header, the menu and every breadcrumb, and /workspace itself redirects to My LCA (confirm, since today it is the only home for auditors and one-event directors). The alternatives are the Int-B (/my/...) or Int-C (/work/...) prefixes with redirects. And the admin's word is 'Admin', as Nav-IA-Final says, not 'Admin panel'.

Officers and the president: withdraw the view-only admin panel and give them rooms for what they can actually do (Support tickets at /workspace/tickets, governance editing in place on the About tabs, Email the members at /workspace/email for the president, the lookup), so only lca_admin ever opens /admin. Default drawn: withdrawn. The alternative is a single 'Admin (view only)' row for them as today, which keeps the members table, payments and the audit log readable by the secretary.

Question 20, the club's named rep: keep club_rep as the club's named author who writes the club's own page and posts its news (your page 9 note on Tue, Oct 13), drawn on Account-S as 'Your club' opening /workspace/region/clubs/:id scoped to one club; or retire the role as P2.18 proposes. If kept, do they also create the club's events and name its TD, or does that stay with the region's representative (P2.19)? Account-S draws the section both ways.

The tournament_director role: keep it as 'a director who can also look up members' (its only difference from a per-event assignment in canManageTournament), drawn as the same section with one lookup line; or fold it into per-event assignments plus lca_auditor for the lookup. And may a standing TD start an event draft and submit it for admin review? Default drawn: no, directors are named only; admins and the region's representative create events.

The treasurer: does the role need the members export or the payments list for dues? Default drawn: the lookup (name, status, end date) inline and a yearly membership count line; export and payments stay admin-only. Confirm too that the member lookup never returns a contact detail (email, phone, address) to TDs, auditors or officers.

The Today list for a plain member: one list named 'Today' holding the personal items (the default, so the page reads the same for everyone), or WS13's 'Needs attention' row with no Today heading until a second role appears. And the header count: personal items only, as WS02 decided (the default), or Int-C's second count for volunteer work ('Your work · 6').

The LCA admin section inside My LCA: a summary with the queue by source, the items assigned to you, the automations line and three shortcuts (the default, so an admin starts the day without opening /admin), or a single row 'Admin · 12 need attention'. In Today the admin sees the queue as one line plus items assigned by name; confirm, or ask for the top three queue items inline. An open regional seat's clubs fall to admins (P2.16) as queue items, with no Representative section on the admin's page; confirm.

Which decisions may be taken inline on My LCA without opening a room: the default is one-tap decisions and confirmations only (approve or decline a bye, email a reminder, 'Still accurate' per club, Add to calendar, Pay); anything with a form (a reply, a schedule change, a result) opens the room.

Collapsible sections with the collapsed state remembered per device (WS13's own risk note), and the default order for a heavy volunteer: Today · You · Family · Events you direct · Your region · Board · LCA admin · Member lookup, the chips in the same order, with a live event's section rising under Today on the day. Default: yes, and that order.

Two things on Account-C that the brief and the code do not hold, dropped from the boards unless you want them: the 'Daily digest · one email at 6:30 AM' toggle (Work-C's weekday 7:00 AM queue digest is the admin's and WS10's Monday digest is public; a per-person digest would be new WS13 scope) and the 'Vote open' item (no vote exists anywhere; the Board section carries the inbox, the next meeting and the documents; votes would be WS14 scope).

On event day the hub never becomes the console: My LCA pins the live event under Today and the strip's TD console button opens /workspace/tournaments/:id/live, whose band reads 'My LCA › The Baton Rouge Classic › Event day' with Exit console. Default: as drawn; say so if you want the console to take over the hub for the day.

Family on Account-I and J: the event-day view sits inside the Family section (as on Account-B) rather than as its own section, and 'Text me' stays hidden until SMS exists (D8). Confirm. And the 'Role looks wrong?' link under the chips opens the contact form with the subject 'My roles' to the admins; default: keep it.

The second factor: admins keep aal2 for /admin; TDs, representatives, officers and auditors keep password-only sessions for their rooms (auth.ts lines 270 to 274 say why). Confirm this stays when officers gain the tickets room and the president the email room, since group email reaches every member.

boards.title: Integration · Int-A · The hub and its rooms (round 2)
boards.name: The hub and its rooms: My LCA holds every role as a section, each section opens its working room, the word Workspace goes
boards.idea: One home at /dashboard for everyone: each grant a person holds adds one section to My LCA that summarises its work, takes one-tap decisions inline and opens its room with one button, while the rooms keep the decided /workspace and /board paths under a 'My LCA › ...' crumb and only lca_admin ever sees /admin.
boards.differs: Against Int-B there is no left rail and no area: one long page with buttons out to the rooms, and the rooms stay separate full-width pages at today's paths. Against Int-C there is no second home: a volunteer's roles live on My LCA itself, so Chris's Monday is one list on one page.
boards.keeps: From Account-C: the role sections (You, Family, Events you direct, Board, now plus Your region, LCA admin and Member lookup), the merged Today list, the On this page rail with counts, the chips, one button per section into its room, and the line 'Admin keeps its own area and never mixes into this page'. From Nav-IA-Final: the 1280px bar, the My LCA ▾ menu order (to-dos, My LCA, the event line, Family, Membership card, rooms by role, Log out), the personal to-do count on the trigger, /dashboard as My LCA, and every decided /workspace/* and /board/inbox path, so WS08, WS09 and WS14 build as written.
boards.removes: The word Workspace from the header, the menu, every crumb and every room title; Account-C's 'Shortcuts into Workspace' box, 'Open Workspace' button and 'Workspace home' link (each section's own button does the job); Account-C's Daily digest toggle and 'Vote open' row (neither exists in the brief or the code); the view-only Admin panel for officers and the president (withdrawn, open for K); Nav-IA-Final's two rows 'Workspace /workspace' and 'My region's clubs /dashboard', replaced by named rooms with counts in words.
boards.spec:
CANVAS. 1440 wide, target height about 3230 (hard cap 3400), page 'account', placed right of Account-C. Draw structure the way Nav-IA-Final draws it: a navy title block, a notes-and-legend row, then lettered sections A to E as labelled frames on the #ecebe6 board ground (padding 40px 48px 56px; content width 1344). Nothing on this board is a page mock-up except the chrome pieces (the bar, the open menu, the crumb bands, one phone sheet). Type Geist, routes in Geist Mono. Gold #c8a94a only as fills with navy text or as rules; gold text on light grounds is gold-ink #705718. Every status in words beside its tint; every date with its weekday; times as '9:10 AM'; 'US Chess' always. Drawn moment unless a cell says otherwise: Mon, Oct 5, 2026 · 9:10 AM. Target heights: title 190 · legend row 300 · A 1180 · B 480 · C 440 · D 300 · E 190, with 36px between sections. If the board runs over 3400, drop cell A9 into section B's redirects strip.

TITLE BLOCK (1344 × 190, #1a2744, radius 14, 4px #c8a94a bottom rule). Kicker in #e6cf86, 12px caps: 'INTEGRATION · ROUND 2 · OPTION INT-A'. H1 34px white: 'The hub and its rooms'. Definition rows (dt #e6cf86 600, dd white, 14.5px): 'Built from' · 'Account-C (one account, many roles) and Nav-IA-Final (the decided structure): the sections stay, the word Workspace goes, every room opens from its section.' 'Replaces' · 'Nothing yet. Int-A, B and C are the options; the section boards Account-D to S and the screen boards Work-E to L are drawn inside Int-A.' 'Source' · 'K, Tue, Oct 13, 2026 (pages 14 and 15) · WS02, WS08, WS13 in docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md · replan 4.2, 4.6, 4.8 · routes checked against src/App.tsx lines 113 to 133 and src/components/layout/Navbar.tsx useAccountLinks.' Right side, top-aligned: a 'Sample data' pill (gold fill, navy text) and a 300px note in white 80%: 'Counts, the sub-lines, the three named volunteers in cells A4 to A6 and their seats are invented. Every route, role rule and label is real, or carries the tag Proposed.'

LEGEND ROW (two boxes, 1fr and 440px, #fbfaf6, 1px #d9d8d1, radius 12, about 300 tall).
Left box, heading 'Notes on this board', six numbered gold circles (navy digits) in two columns, 13.5px:
1 One home at /dashboard, labelled My LCA, for everyone signed in. A plain member sees the You section only: no chips, no role rows, nothing that hints at volunteer work.
2 Each grant adds one section (Family, Events you direct, Your region, Board, LCA admin, Member lookup). A section summarises its work, takes one-tap decisions inline and opens its room with one button.
3 The rooms keep the decided paths (/workspace/..., /board/inbox) so WS08, WS09 and WS14 build as written, but no page title, menu row or crumb says Workspace. A room is named for what it is (Setup, Event day, Recap, My region, Board inbox, Support tickets, Member lookup) and carries 'My LCA › ...' above it.
4 Admin stays a separate area at /admin, for lca_admin with a second factor. Officers and the president get rooms for what they can actually do and never open /admin (Q3, open for K).
5 The My LCA ▾ menu keeps the WS02 order. The one row 'Workspace / Admin / Board inbox / My region's clubs by role' becomes named rooms, each with its count in words. The trigger count stays personal (src/lib/todo.ts, not yet in the tree).

boards.idea: My LCA stops being one page and becomes a small area under /my with a persistent left rail, one entry per grant the person holds, where the working screens (the console, the checklist, My region, the inbox, tickets, email) are pages inside the same shell, so there is no 'summary here, work there' step.
boards.differs: Against Int-A the roles are rail entries and short pages instead of sections on one long page, and the console, checklist, My region and inbox render inside the My LCA shell under /my/... instead of as separate rooms under /workspace/...; against Int-C there is one home with a rail, not two homes, and the menu carries no second count.

From Nav-IA-Final: the 1280px bar, the trigger with the personal count, the short menu (to-dos, My LCA, the event line, Family, Membership card, Admin for lca_admin, Log out), /admin as a separate area with its grouped sidebar, and the event strip's deep link.

boards.name: One column, the card is a section
boards.idea: The plain member's page is one column in WS13 order, Today first, and the membership card lives inside the Membership section with the US Chess status beside it, so the page reads top to bottom with nothing floating.
boards.differs: Where the card lives: on D it is a section the rail jumps to; on E it sits in a sticky side column; on F it is the page's navy header band. Everything else on the three boards is the same page.
boards.keeps: From Account-A: Avery, Needs attention as the top list, the date-ordered Next up with the four-step tracker and Pay · Change section · Byes · Withdraw, the card with its QR, the US Chess block with the nightly check, the receipts, History and the Settings cards. From Account-C: the On this page rail, now listing the You section's own parts.
boards.removes: Role chips (none below two roles), Shortcuts into Workspace, the daily digest, every Text control (D8), the club night as a dated row and the 'Home club' line (K, page 9: no computed club dates), 'member entry discounts' (D11), the Wallet buttons (wait for D4), milestones and the calendar feed (not in WS13).

THE RULES THE BOARD DRAWS (print as a 12px grey panel at the right of Frame 3, 240 wide, under the insets). An item is something the viewer can finish or decide today, from this page or one of its rooms, with a deadline within 14 days or a person waiting on the viewer now; it carries exactly one button in words. A status, a count of things that are fine, or information with no action is never an item. Tiers: 1 due today or already past; 2 money and eligibility with a date, in WS13's order (unpaid entry, US Chess before an entered event, LCA membership within 30 days, a waitlist offer), then the nearer date first; 3 a person waiting on you, longest wait first; 4 dated upkeep, sooner deadline first, undated last; 5 counts and summaries (an admin's queue line only). Inside a tier: sooner deadline, then the role order You · Family · Director · Representative · Board · Admin. Cap: seven open; the rest behind 'Show N more', and no role may hold more than three rows before the fold. The header's My LCA count stays the personal count; volunteer items never count there.

boards.differs: Account-K lists events as dense rows with the next step as a sentence; Account-L gives each event a card with a five-stage track so a director sees at a glance which stage each event is in.
boards.keeps: From Account-C: the same events, counts by section, flags, the inline bye decision and reminder email, the rating report check, the way into the console. From Work-D: the 10-step setup and its progress; from Work-A and replan 4.6: the results queue counts, the close-out and the rating report step.
boards.removes: Account-C's 'Add a co-director', 'Manage' as a label, the Workspace link, the digest toggle, the vote rows; and the single next-step sentence (the current stage's panel carries what is left instead).

boards.idea: The section leads with what needs doing in the region: the clubs not checked in 90 days with one-tap Still accurate, the open reports with their age in words, the club events in review, then the monthly check line and the buttons into My region.
boards.differs: Account-N leads with every club in the region as a tile (the region at a glance) and lists the tasks under the grid; Account-M leads with the tasks and names the healthy clubs in one line.
boards.keeps: From Account-C's club block: the 'Is this still accurate?' one-tap confirm with 'Still right' as Still accurate, 'Confirm all', the Post club news and Add a club event actions, the representative line with the seat. From Work-B: the visitor report with its reply options and the 14-day rule, the Tonight switch and the schedule editor (now in the room), club events behind LCA review.
boards.removes: Everything Work-B and Account-C held for one club's own manager: the members table and renewal reminders, the QR sign-in, the followers count, page views, 'members list it as their home club', co-representatives, the Tonight switch and schedule editor drawn inline (they live in the room); the 'Daily digest' toggle; computed next-meeting dates (a club states how it meets in its own words).

Weekday on every date, '7:00 PM', '½', 'US Chess', status words beside tints. Four page excerpts stacked, each a cropped My LCA at 1280 wide (x 80 to 1360) with the page head, the rail, Today and the one section; the decided header is drawn once on excerpt B (where the event strip matters) and implied on the others by a 12px grey line 'the decided header, Donate · My LCA ▾, as on every page'. Board height: about 2560px.

DRAWN MOMENT. Mon, Oct 5, 2026, 8:40 AM for all four. Badge at the top: 'Sample data · Lila Guidry, Gerald Prejean and every count, ticket and time are invented; Tommy LeBlanc, Paul Comeaux, the clubs, events, routes, roles and seat names come from the boards and the code'.

REGION 1 · BOARD TITLE BLOCK (x 80, y 60 to 190). Title 'My LCA · S · The small roles: auditor, one-event director, president, club rep (round 2)', 28px navy 700. Line 2, 15px grey: 'Grows from Account-C and Work-B. Four people who hold one small grant each. Each excerpt shows the chips, the Today list, the section, its rail row and its menu row.' Line 3, the Frame line in a cream box with a 1px #866a1e rule: 'Drawn inside Int-A (My LCA as the hub, rooms open from each section). The frame is swappable: under Int-B this section is the page the left rail opens; under Int-C it is a card on Your work. The room itself does not change; only the breadcrumb, the way back and the menu row do. Pick the frame on Account-Int-A, B or C.'

EXCERPT ANATOMY (shared by A to D). A white card 1280 wide with a 1px #e8e8e3 border and a navy tab at its top left reading the letter and the role ('A · LCA auditor'). Inside: the page head (name 28px navy 700, chips, the 'no modes' line with 'Role looks wrong?'), then three columns: the rail (x 104, w 200: 'ON THIS PAGE' with its rows), the main column (x 328, w 700: the Today card, then the section), and a right column (x 1052, w 284) holding two insets: 'Menu row' (the My LCA ▾ menu at 1:1, the section's row ringed in gold) and 'Empty state' (the section's empty copy in a small card). The rail's current row is the section's row.

REGION 6 · LEGEND (y 2430 to 2540), six notes:
1. Four grants, four small sections, one page shape: nothing on any of these pages reads Workspace or Admin, and each section opens its one room (/workspace/lookup, the setup checklist, /board/inbox and /workspace/email, /workspace/region/clubs/:id).
2. The Today heading rule shown three ways: 'Today' with nothing (A), 'Today across your roles · 4 things · 1 is yours' with labels (B), 'Today' with one role and no labels (C, D).
3. The auditor never has an item and never writes; the lookup answers name, status in words and the end date only.
4. A one-event director gets the row and the rooms, never the lookup; the membership switch, naming directors and deleting stay with admins and the representative.
5. The president's two extra lines (Email the members, Email entrants) are the whole difference from an officer; the read-only reach over every seat, club and event is today's and is open for K.
6. The club rep card is drawn both ways for events and marked 'only if K keeps the role'; while the Bayou Region seat is open, admins are the backstop (P2.16).

boards.title: Workspace · E · TD console, one stage at a time (round 2)
boards.name: TD console · one stage at a time
boards.idea: The console shows one stage at a time, picked from the rail (check-in, a round's results, Hall TV, close-out); the current stage fills the width under the Next step strip, so a TD at a tablet never scrolls past work that is not now.
boards.differs: Work-E switches stages one at a time at full width; Work-F puts every panel on one scrolled page in two columns.
boards.keeps: From Work-A: the navy status band, the round rail, the gated Next step (confirm, pair, publish and notify), the 64px check-in rows with scan sources and undo, the tap results grid with keyboard entry, Print and QR, Announcements with a sent log, the rating report checks, the offline badge, Exit console top right.
boards.removes: The countdown ('in 16 minutes': absolute times only, per Nav-Header-Final Q16), every 'texted' line and the Text channel (D8), the club on check-in rows (D17), the word Workspace in the crumb, the three Next step cards (now one strip), the separate rating report card (now the Close-out stage).

FRAME A, 1440 wide, about 1500 tall. Top: the decided signed-in header (rook mark, six sections, Search ⌘K, Donate · My LCA ▾ with the personal count 1: Ella's November Meet entry unpaid). No event strip on the console: the band carries the Players see line itself. Crumb line, 44px, cream: 'My LCA › Events you direct › The Baton Rouge Classic › Event day', every crumb a link (/dashboard, /dashboard#directing, /tournaments/the-baton-rouge-classic); right end a bordered 'Exit console' (to /dashboard#directing). Status band, navy #1a2744, 150px: kicker 'EVENT DAY · SAT, OCT 24 · 9:31 PM' in light gold #e6cf86; title 'The Baton Rouge Classic' 34px white; sub-line 'Baton Rouge · 26 players · 4 sections · 5 rounds · G/90+30 (90 min each + 30 sec per move)'; right block 'Round 4 starts' 'Sun, Oct 25 · 9:30 AM' (no countdown), buttons 'Hall TV' and 'Public page' (ghost on navy); below the title, 'Players see: Round 3 in progress · 8 of 13 results confirmed'. Sync pill at the band's foot: 'Saved on this tablet · synced 9:31 PM · keeps working if the venue Wi-Fi drops'; offline variant 'Offline · 3 changes waiting · retrying' in amber #f3eedc with navy text.
Stage rail, under the band, 8 tabs of 48px with a 4px top rule each (done #8fa3c9, now gold #c8a94a with the word 'Now' beside the label, later #3a4a6e): 'Check-in · Closed Sat 9:52 AM' · 'Round 1 · Done' · 'Round 2 · Done' · 'Round 3 · 8 of 13 confirmed · Now' · 'Round 4 · Sun 9:30 AM' · 'Round 5 · Sun 2:00 PM' · 'Hall TV · All on one screen' · 'Close-out · after round 5'. Tapping a tab shows that stage alone; the rail never scrolls sideways (it wraps to two rows under 1100px).
Next step strip, white card, three numbered pills left to right: '1 Confirm round 3 results · 5 left' (navy, live), '2 Pair round 4 · unlocks when every round 3 result is confirmed' (grey), '3 Publish round 4 and notify · unlocks after pairing' (grey). One sentence under it: 'Confirm, pair, publish. One big button at a time.'
THE STAGE 'Round 3 · results'. Card 1, Reported results queue: heading 'Reported results · Round 3 · 3 to check'; sub 'Players' reports steer you; they never set a result. Disagreements first, then oldest first.'; counts in words with a three-part bar: '8 of 13 confirmed · 3 reported, waiting · 2 not reported' (navy, gold, grey, each labelled). Three rows, each 2 lines plus 56px buttons: Board 2 · Open · W Jean-Paul Fontenot 2011 · B Kevin Tran 1942 · '1–0 White reported 9:20 PM' · '½–½ Black reported 9:21 PM' · tag 'Reports disagree' (red tint #fbe9e7, red text) 'Each says something different. Foot: 'Not reported yet: boards 11 and 13 (U1000). Results you enter below or from a paper sheet skip this queue. · Reporting history for this round'.
Card 2, Results grid, all sections: section chips 'All sections 13 · Open 4 · U1800 3 · U1400 3 · U1000 3 · Needs a look 3'; hint 'Tap a result. With a keyboard: 1 White wins, 2 draw, 3 Black wins, arrows move between boards. Press and hold for forfeits.'; table Bd · Section · White · Result · Black · Status · Action, 13 rows at 56px, result as three 48px buttons 1–0 · ½–½ · 0–1 with the chosen one filled navy: 1 Open Marcus Landry 1–0 Priya Shah Confirmed by TD Edit · 2 Open Jean-Paul Fontenot (blank) Kevin Tran Reports disagree Review · 3 Open Neil Robichaux ½–½ Luke Arceneaux Confirmed by TD Edit · 4 Open Avery Thibodeaux 0–1 Ravi Menon Confirmed by TD Edit · 5 U1800 Camille Broussard 1–0 Nora Hebert Confirmed by TD Edit · 6 U1800 Devin Batiste (blank) Elise Fontenot Reported by Black Review · 7 U1800 Isaac Dupre ½–½ Lauren Guillory Confirmed by TD Edit · 8 U1400 Olivia Landreneau 1–0 Rosa Mendez Confirmed by TD Edit · 9 U1400 Jordan Lee (blank) Maya Robichaux Reported by White Review · 10 U1400 Theo Guidry 0–1 Andre Charbonnet Confirmed by TD Edit · 11 U1000 Sofia Alvarez (blank) Lily Nguyen Not reported Enter · 12 U1000 Ben Landry 1–0 Mateo Reyes Confirmed by TD Edit · 13 U1000 Khadija Williams (blank) Tommy Pham Not reported Enter. Status words sit beside their tint, never colour alone. Foot: 'Last change 9:29 PM · board 10 · Undo' and 'Public pages show 8 results; boards 2, 6, 9, 11 and 13 stay blank until you confirm.'
Inset A1 (right of the grid, 420 wide): the 'Enter a different result' sheet for board 2: both reports listed with names and times, the TD's entry under them (1–0 · ½–½ · 0–1 · White forfeit · Black forfeit), an optional note, 'Save, final'. Line: 'Both reports stay on the record. Nothing is deleted.'

FRAME B (left half, 700 wide, scaled): the Check-in stage on Sun, Oct 25, 9:14 AM, Round 4. Counts 21 Here · 2 Byes · 2 Not here yet · 1 Withdrew; search 'Name, US Chess ID or parent's name'; 'Scan a card'; chips All 26 · Needs a look 5 · Not here 2 · Byes 2 · US Chess flags 1; rows 64px, one action each: Isaac Dupre · 1688 · U1800 · ID ending 8264 · 1½ pts · emailed 9:05 AM · Not here · Check in; Rosa Mendez · 1219 · U1400 · ID ending 2917 · 1½ pts · 'US Chess ended Mon, Oct 12' · Not here · Check in; Nora Hebert · 1577 · U1800 · bye ½ point requested Sat · Cancel bye; Theo Guidry · 1295 · U1400 · bye ½ point requested at registration · Cancel bye; Sam Nguyen · 1650 · U1800 · withdrew Sat 11:40 PM · Undo; Maya Robichaux · 1102 · U1400 · 2 pts · Robichaux family · Danielle Robichaux · 8:47 AM · scanned the door QR · Here · Undo; Avery Thibodeaux · 1912 · Open · 8:51 AM · wallet card scanned at the desk · Here · Undo; Jordan Lee · 1388 · U1400 · 8:58 AM · tapped in by the TD · Here · Undo. FRAME C (right half, 700 wide): the Close-out stage on Sun, Oct 25, 5:40 PM, after round 5. Heading 'Close out the event: US Chess rating report · due Sun, Nov 1, 2026, 7 days after the last round' · tag 'Not yet tested with US Chess'. Checks with 'Passed' in words: every result confirmed by a TD, no reports waiting · all results entered in 4 sections, 1 forfeit marked and left out of rating · US Chess IDs on file and memberships current for 25 of 26 players: 'Rosa Mendez's membership ended Mon, Oct 12 · Email her the renewal link' (not passed, amber) · bye limits respected · affiliate ID, Chief TD's US Chess ID, city, state and ZIP filled in. The three files: THEXPORT.DBF 'Ready · 1 record', TSEXPORT.DBF 'Ready · 4 records', TDEXPORT.DBF 'Held · fix the check above' ; 'Download all three (.zip)' greyed with the reason in words. 'Test this file before a real event' box with the four steps and the SwissSys drop box; then 'Mark as submitted to US Chess', 'Send the one-page final report to the LCA board', 'Mark as completed', and 'Recap tab · opens when standings are final'.
FRAME D (small, 480 wide, under C): Hall TV settings, Sat, Oct 24, 2:05 PM: 'Show sections: One at a time, cycling every 15 seconds · All on one screen (Suggested: 26 players, 13 boards fit)', each with a small layout picture; 'Show standings after results come in' on; 'TD keys: Space pauses, arrows step, A all on one screen, S standings now'; 'Open the TV screen'. Variant line: at 96 players 'All on one screen' greyed: 'Too many boards for one screen (16 at most)'.
FRAME E (480 wide): the Round 3 stage at 1024×768: band condensed to 96px, rail in two rows, queue buttons stacked under each row, grid result buttons 48px; nothing scrolls sideways.
STATES strip under the frames: Empty: a round with no reports yet, queue reads 'No reports yet for Round 4. Results you enter below go straight in.' and every grid row 'Not reported'. Busy: 6 reports waiting with two disagreements; the queue shows five and 'Show 1 more'. Offline: the pill reads 'Offline · 3 changes waiting' and the Publish button 'Publishes when the Wi-Fi is back'.
WAY IN AND BACK inset: the My LCA ▾ menu row 'The Baton Rouge Classic · Open event day' and the strip 'Live · Round 3 · The Baton Rouge Classic · 8 of 13 results confirmed · 3 reports waiting · [TD console] · Players see: Round 3 in progress'; the Events you direct row's 'Event day' button; Exit console and every crumb go back; after 'Publish round 4 and notify' a line 'Done · Back to My LCA'. Three crumbs side by side: 'My LCA › Events you direct › The Baton Rouge Classic › Event day' (Int-A) · 'My LCA rail › The Baton Rouge Classic › Event day' (Int-B, /my/events/:id/live) · 'My LCA › Your work › The Baton Rouge Classic › Event day' (Int-C, /work/tournaments/:id/live).
LEGEND, six notes: 1 One stage at a time: the rail picks it, the Next step strip stays above every stage. 2 Reports steer, never set: one report lands at once, disagreements first, the TD confirms in one tap or enters a different result; both reports stay on the record. 3 Status in words on every board; the public sees only confirmed results. 4 Check-in rows: full name, section, rating, ID ending, household, no club; one action each, 64px. 5 Close-out: five checks in words, three named files, the test record, Mark as submitted (due Sun, Nov 1), Mark as completed, then the Recap tab. 6 Works at 1024×768 with nothing sideways; the tablet keeps a copy and syncs. Frame line: 'Drawn inside Int-A (My LCA as the hub, rooms open from each section). The frame is swappable: under Int-B this room is the page the left rail opens; under Int-C it opens from a card on Your work. The room itself does not change; only the breadcrumb, the way back and the menu row do. Pick the frame on Account-Int-A, B or C.' Standing rules: weekday on every date, times as '9:30 AM', ½, 'US Chess', words beside colour, gold never as text on light, no em dashes.

boards.title: Workspace · K · Setup checklist, every step on one page (round 2)
boards.name: Setup checklist · every step on one page
boards.idea: All ten setup steps sit on one form that scrolls in its own container, with the steps rail and the page preview pinned beside it; an experienced director sees and fixes anything in one scroll.
boards.differs: Work-K shows every step on one page; Work-L shows one step at a time with Back and Save and continue.

boards.spec:
CANVAS 1440 wide, under 3400. Title strip: the title · Built from Work-D, Event-Final-Setup and WS08 as amended (replan 4.6) · Replaces Work-D, with Work-L · Shown: /workspace/tournaments/2027-paul-morphy-open/setup on Thu, Oct 8, 2026 at 7:40 PM, signed in as Chris Arceneaux, the named director · badge 'Sample data · dates, venue, fees, prizes, caps, room notes' · K's page 15 note verbatim.

EVENT DATA (Sample data, shared with Work-L): 2027 Paul Morphy Open, LCA event, cloned from 2026 with every date moved forward a year onto the same weekday; Sat–Sun, Jun 12–13, 2027; [Venue name], New Orleans; 5-round Swiss, US Chess regular rated, G/90+30 ('90 min each + 30 sec per move'); tagline '[Tagline]' optional, championship title None. Sections with caps (Limits by section, overall 60): Open 15, U1800 20, U1400 15, U1000 10; eligibility 'Everyone' · 'Rated under 1800, or unrated' · 'under 1400, or unrated' · 'under 1000, or unrated'; Where in the room: Open 'Main hall, boards 1–8' · U1800 'Main hall, boards 9–18' · U1400 'Room B, boards 1–8' · U1000 'Room B, boards 9–13'. Fees, one price per section per tier, no member price: Early until Mon, May 31 · Regular Tue, Jun 1 to Thu, Jun 10 · Late from Fri, Jun 11 and at the door: Open $50 · $60 · $70; U1800 $40 · $50 · $60; U1400 $30 · $40 · $50; U1000 $20 · $30 · $40. LCA membership: 'Required to enter · set by LCA admins for LCA events' (locked for a director). Schedule: check-in Sat 8:30–9:30 AM; R1 Sat 10:00 AM; R2 Sat 2:30 PM; R3 Sat 7:00 PM; R4 Sun 9:30 AM; R5 Sun 2:00 PM; Schedules option off. Byes: up to 2 half-point byes; round 5 zero-point only; requests close when Round 2 is paired; lapsed US Chess membership Warn · Warn + email · Block (Warn + email picked). Venue & travel: venue fields filled, travel details off, no hotel. Prizes: 'Copied from 2026: $1,500 based on 60 entries · Confirm' (To do). Side events: off. Directors: Chief TD Chris Arceneaux · US Chess TD ID [needed] · 'Directors are named by LCA admins or the region's representative; a director can't add or remove directors'. Registration: opens Mon, Oct 12, 2026, 9:00 AM; waitlist with a 24-hour claim; 'Show X of 60 registered'; family checkout on. Publish: display Automatic; the share card; 'Publish Mon, Oct 12, 9:00 AM' scheduled, 'Post it to LCA News' and 'Email members who follow New Orleans Metro events' ticked; status 'Draft · publishes when Prizes and Directors are done'. Steps rail: 8 of 10 done; Prizes and Directors To do.

FRAME A, 1440 wide, about 2300 tall: the decided signed-in header (My LCA ▾ count 1). Crumb 'My LCA › Events you direct › 2027 Paul Morphy Open › Setup', right 'Back to My LCA'. Band: tags 'Draft · LCA event'; title '2027 Paul Morphy Open'; 'Saved 7:38 PM · Chris Arceneaux, tournament director · leave any time and pick up where you stopped'; right 'Preview public page' · 'Save draft' · 'Publish' (gold, greyed until steps 7 and 9 are done, with the reason in words). The clone banner: 'Started from the 2026 Paul Morphy Open. Sections, fees, schedule, byes and prizes were copied and every date moved forward a year onto the same weekday. Check anything marked To do. · Undo · Start from another event'. Then the two-column body: the form, 900 wide, scrolls in its own container (D16; a 2px inner shadow at its top and bottom edges shows it scrolls); the right column, 440 wide, is sticky. The form, ten numbered cards in order, each with a status word at its head (Done · To do · 1 note · Last step): 1 Basics (dates, where, type, format, time control, tagline, championship title None). 2 Sections: quick-add chips Open · U1800 · U1400 · U1000 and K–12 · K–8 · K–5 · K–3, 'Entry limit: Overall · Limits by section (picked)', the table Section · Who can enter · Cap · Where in the room (a short text per row, hint 'Shown on each player's pinned Your game card, such as Room B, boards 1–8') · Order; 'Scholastic presets ask one yes/no question, never a grade or birthdate.' 3 Fees: the timeline Early · Regular · Late with weekday dates, the 4×3 price grid, 'One price per section per tier. There is no member price.', then 'LCA membership · Required to enter · Not required', drawn locked with 'Set by LCA admins for LCA events. A club's own event may switch it off, by the region's representative or an admin.' 4 Schedule: the six rows with weekdays and times, the 'Tight turnarounds' note ('At G/90+30 a 60-move game can run about 4 hours, so Rounds 2, 3 and 5 may start just 30 minutes after the longest game ends · Keep as is · Add 30 min to each gap'), 'Schedules · Off · a second schedule with its own rounds and merge round'. 5 Byes & rules (the four rows). 6 Venue & travel (venue name, address, parking, getting in, food; 'Travel details · Off'; 'Add a hotel'). 7 Prizes (To do, Confirm prizes). 8 Side events (Off · Add a side event or meeting). 9 Directors (To do, the Chief TD line and the naming rule). 10 Publish: 'The page shows · Automatic · Before · During · After', the share card (kicker, title, 'Sat–Sun, Jun 12–13, 2027 · New Orleans', 'Register · from $20'), 'louisianachess.org/t/2027-paul-morphy-open · Copy', the three publish boxes, 'Publish now · Publish Mon, Oct 12, 9:00 AM'. Right column: 'Setup steps · 8 of 10 done' list with each step's status word; 'Live preview · Event card · Phone' (the card: '12 Jun · 2027 Paul Morphy Open · Sat–Sun, Jun 12–13, 2027 · New Orleans · LCA event · Opens Mon, Oct 12 · Open · U1800 · U1400 · U1000 · 5 rounds · G/90+30 · From $20, early until Mon, May 31 · 0 of 60 registered · Waitlist when full · LCA membership required to enter'); 'Link preview · Facebook, Messages, Discord' with the server-rendered card and the 'Loading tournament details…' counterexample line.
INSET K1 (560 wide, under the frame): the same Fees step on a club event, Baton Rouge Chess Club November Saturday G/90, signed in as Chris as the region's representative on Mon, Oct 5, 8:50 AM: the switch is live, 'Not required' picked, line 'Club events may drop it; the checkout then skips the membership step', and the band reads 'Submit for LCA review' in place of Publish with 'LCA admins review club events before they go public; you'll get an email.' INSET K2 (400 wide): a new event with nothing cloned: every step To do, the preview a schematic with 'Always' blocks, the banner 'Start from a past event · or fill the steps in order'. INSET K3 (400 wide): a live event with 23 registered: a change that strands paid players is stopped in words: 'Dropping U1000 would strand 3 paid players. Move them first from Entries.'
STATES: Empty is K2; busy is K3 (live, 23 registered, every step editable, 'Published Mon, Sep 28, 2026').
WAY IN AND BACK inset: the Events you direct row's 'Setup' button ('Setup 8 of 10'); the Today item 'Director · 2027 Paul Morphy Open · Next: confirm the prize list · Open setup'; for a new event, Admin › Tournaments › New tournament or My region › the club › Events › Add a club event (/workspace/tournaments/new?club=); 'Back to My LCA' in the band; after Publish, 'Done · Back to My LCA'. Three crumbs: 'My LCA › Events you direct › 2027 Paul Morphy Open › Setup' (Int-A) · 'My LCA rail › 2027 Paul Morphy Open › Setup' (Int-B, /my/events/:id/setup) · 'My LCA › Your work › 2027 Paul Morphy Open › Setup' (Int-C, /work/tournaments/:id/setup).
LEGEND, six notes: 1 Every step on one page; the form scrolls in its own container with the rail and preview pinned (D16). 2 Start from last year: copies and moves every date a year forward onto the same weekday. 3 One price per section per tier, no member price (D11); LCA membership required by default, switched off only on a club's event by the representative or an admin (D12). 4 'Where in the room' per section reaches each player's pinned Your game card. 5 Directors are named by admins or the region's representative; a director finishes every step but the membership switch. 6 Club events submit for LCA review; LCA events publish now or on a date. Frame line: 'Drawn inside Int-A ... The room itself does not change; only the breadcrumb, the way back and the menu row do. Pick the frame on Account-Int-A, B or C.'

boards.differs: Work-L shows one step at a time with Back and Save and continue; Work-K shows every step on one scrolling page.
boards.keeps: Everything Work-K keeps from Work-D, and the same ten steps, data and rules.
boards.removes: The same as Work-K, and the single long form: no step is drawn beside another.

CANVAS, title strip, event data, header, insets K1 to K3, states, the three breadcrumbs and the frame line are Work-K's; only the layout differs. Shown: the same event on Thu, Oct 8, 2026 at 7:40 PM, Chris Arceneaux, on step 2.

FRAME A, 1440 wide, about 1500 tall: crumb 'My LCA › Events you direct › 2027 Paul Morphy Open › Setup', 'Back to My LCA'; the band as Work-K with 'Step 2 of 10 · Sections' under the title and the clone banner folded to one line 'Started from the 2026 Paul Morphy Open · dates moved a year · Undo'. Three columns: the rail, 260 wide, lists the ten steps with status words (1 Basics Done · 2 Sections Now · 3 Fees Done · 4 Schedule 1 note · 5 Byes & rules Done · 6 Venue & travel Done · 7 Prizes To do · 8 Side events Off · 9 Directors To do · 10 Publish Last step), any step tappable, the current one with a gold-ink bar and aria-current; the step, 760 wide: 'Sections' with Work-K's chips, the entry-limit choice, the table with Cap and Where in the room, the scholastic line, and at its foot a 56px bar 'Back · Skip for now (marks To do) · Save and continue'; the preview, 360 wide, sticky: the event card redrawn from the step ('Open · U1800 · U1400 · U1000 · 0 of 60 registered') and under it 'What this step changes on the page: the section cards, the count line, the section picker, the Your game card's room line'. Under the step, full width of the middle column, a 'Jump to' line of the ten step numbers.
FRAME B (two insets of 560 wide, side by side): step 3 Fees, one step alone, with the locked membership switch and the line 'Set by LCA admins for LCA events'; and step 10 Publish, with the steps summary ('8 of 10 done · Prizes and Directors still To do'), the share card, the display choice and 'Publish Mon, Oct 12, 9:00 AM' greyed with the reason in words.
FRAME C (400 wide): the rail on a tablet at 1024: the steps become a top row of numbered chips with the current one named ('2 · Sections'); the preview drops under the step.
INSETS K1 to K3 as Work-K (the representative's club event with the switch live and 'Submit for LCA review'; the new event with every step To do; the live event's stranded-players stop).
WAY IN AND BACK as Work-K; the Events you direct row's 'Setup' button opens the first step still To do ('Setup 8 of 10' opens step 7 Prizes).
LEGEND, six notes: 1 One step at a time, led by the rail; Back and Save and continue; Skip marks To do. 2 Start from last year (as Work-K note 2). 3 No member price; the membership switch (as Work-K note 3). 4 Where in the room (as Work-K note 4). 5 The preview shows what the current step changes on the page. 6 Trade-off in words: guided for a first-time director, slower for an experienced one who wants everything in one scroll; the rail still jumps anywhere. Frame line as Work-K.
